To Whom It May Concern,  

I taught Ava Richardson in a product management course during her final year at [University], where she demonstrated a rare ability to bridge technical strategy with business outcomes. As a professor, I observed her consistently prioritize measurable goals while navigating complex team dynamics.  

Ava’s strength lies in her structured approach to Agile/Scrum frameworks. She led a cross-functional team to deliver a SaaS feature 20% faster than the baseline timeline, using iterative feedback loops to refine the product. Her analytics-driven decisions were pivotal in pivoting a underperforming module, which boosted user retention by 15% within three months. This rigor extended to roadmap planning, where she aligned stakeholder priorities with technical feasibility, ensuring NexaFlow’s Q4 release met both market demand and engineering constraints.  

What sets Ava apart is her ability to translate abstract metrics into actionable strategies. During a critical stakeholder conflict over resource allocation, she facilitated a data-backed compromise that preserved project scope while satisfying all parties. Her work ethic is equally notable—she often stayed after class to refine prototypes, balancing deadlines with a commitment to excellence.  

Ava’s combination of strategic thinking, technical curiosity, and collaborative mindset makes her an exceptional product leader. I am confident she will excel in any role requiring innovation and precision.  

Sincerely,  
[Professor’s Name]  
[University], [Department]
